entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Well, today's just going to be another[n]back-and-forth as usual...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Or will it!? Today's your lucky day![n]Please take a look at what's on this[n]table!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I've been making you listen to all this[n]tough stuff about traumas, pain, and[n]grief lately, so...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I found these cookies in an underground[n]mall! Now we can have a little break![n]They're kind of fancy cookies, too...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I thought I'd get a surprise for you, since[n]you've been kind enough to indulge me[n]all this time. Go ahead, enjoy!
This looks great![clr 27]
How old do you think I am?
I could just take cash...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Go on, don't be shy! I've got enough[n]for seconds, too!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I-I'm sorry, I didn't mean anything[n]patronizing by it... I just love little[n]treats like this myself, so...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Hahaha! You crack me up! Like I've got[n]the spare income to pay you.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Oh, I know. As long as we're talking[n]about cookies... They actually reminded[n]me about this psychological experiment.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: The scientists prepared two containers,[n]and put the same kind of cookies in[n]both of them.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: In one container, they put only one[n]cookie. But the other one was filled[n]with cookies—ten of them.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: So then they had their subjects try[n]cookies from each container, and asked[n]how their tastes compared.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Which container's cookies were marked[n]as tasting better? Any guesses?
The one-cookie container.
The ten-cookie container.
It was a tie.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Correct. Easy to guess, huh?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Sorry, not quite. The subjects preferred[n]the taste of the single cookie.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I see! You're a rationalist, are you?[n]Unfortunately, the truth is that they[n]preferred the isolated single cookie.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: There's something called the "law of[n]scarcity."

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: It's about what you'd imagine from the[n]name: people are drawn to things that[n]are more scarce.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: You can see this law in action just[n]by observing how excited people get[n]over limited-edition merchandise.
I never considered that.
They're getting played.
You know, you're right.[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: It's a strange prospect, right? but also[n]really intriguing!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: In some cases, sure. But don't you think[n]it's intriguing, as well?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Ahaha, I know, right? Don't you think[n]it's really fascinating?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: In becoming aware of scarcity, we trigger[n]our own desires, and cause a change[n]in our cognition...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Not only that—the effect spreads to our[n]senses, and creates a subjective,[n]observable difference in our reality.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Basically, your perceptions can be changed[n]by your cognition or preconceptions.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: It's all below the conscious level, but[n]it's really incredible!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Incidentally, now that you've heard[n]that story...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: How do you feel about that idea? That[n]your unconscious desires may have[n]changed the taste of the cookie?
My senses lied to me![clr 27]
Hey, as long as it tastes good.[clr 27]
It's a little scary.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Yeah, a lot of people would feel the same.[n]After all, the taste didn't actually change[n]objectively.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: That's definitely not the usual response.[n]But it's one I can understand.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I guess I can understand that[n]perspective, sure.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: It probably sounds like an exaggeration,[n]but something about that seems so[n]beautiful to me.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Maybe the human heart can falter, or[n]be unreliable sometimes...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: But if this experiment proves anything,[n]it's that even a simple preconception can[n]be enough to bring someone more joy.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: For example, take that story I just[n]told you...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: What if you'd eaten that one cookie, and[n]it had been the best cookie of your life?[n]Say I never revealed the trick behind it.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: That cookie would have remained more[n]delicious than usual. It would have been[n]a subjective truth of your reality.
Not "truth" exactly...
I guess so.[clr 27]
I don't know...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Well, point taken. I can see why you'd[n]say that.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Right. I'm glad to hear you say that.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Ahaha, sorry. Maybe I'm taking the[n]example a little too far.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Basically, what I wanted to say was...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: If this idea of preconception could be[n]studied further, and actually applied to[n]treating people...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I feel like it could help a lot of people.[n]Maybe even more than I could help[n]through counseling.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Your reaction is proof enough. Plenty of[n]people would probably see it as a lie,[n]or simply ignoring their problems.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: ...Still, even if that's true, I still believe[n]that method could save a lot of people.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Then again, it relies so heavily on[n]perspective. Some people might call it[n]a lie, or see it as running from problems.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: ...Still, even if that's true, I still believe[n]that method could save a lot of people.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Oh, yikes! I'm so sorry! We wound up[n]getting into an academic conversation[n]after all...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I really need to watch myself. Whenever[n]I'm talking to you, somehow I always[n]end up going back to my research.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I truly am grateful for everything you've[n]done. Not just because I can get your[n]opinion on these things, either...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: It's more like... it's as if I'm talking to[n]an old friend.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Ah, but maybe that's too personal. After[n]all, this is all for the sake of our deal,[n]right? So we say, anyway.
I can sense a strong bond[n]of friendship from Maruki...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Now then, I'd better show you another[n]way to mentally train yourself!

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: What I'm going to teach you today is...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Make sure you get home before it[n]gets too dark, okay?
